title: Tournament branch predictor with local, global and chooser
where_in_paper: Branch prediction and sidebar Local and global branch predictors
decision: Implement sophisticated tournament predictor that dynamically chooses between two-level local predictor (1024 entries x 10-bit history -> 1024 prediction counters) and global predictor (4096-entry table indexed by 12-branch path history) via 4096-entry chooser table of 2-bit counters
alternatives_or_rejected: Simple single-level BHT or larger single table of either type alone; paper notes tournament with better accuracy than larger tables of either individual method
rationale: 21264 has higher mispredict cost (7-cycle) and 80 inflight instructions vs 20 in 21164, so efficient fetch and speculation requires 90-100% success; local captures self-correlation, global captures cross-branch correlation, chooser picks best per branch invocation
outcome: Reported 90% to 100% success on most benchmarks, training infrequent, enables continuous stream of good-path instructions despite 4-wide fetch and speculative execution

title: Line and way prediction for instruction cache
where_in_paper: Instruction pipeline - Fetch cache and line and way prediction
decision: Add line and way prediction to 64KB 2-way set-associative I-cache: predict next fetch block address and which way, read next instructions via wraparound path while validity check (decode, branch prediction, tag compare) happens in parallel outside critical fetch loop
alternatives_or_rejected: Wait for tag comparison and branch decode before next fetch, or use 8KB direct-mapped cache as in 21164 to avoid way selection but with lower hit rate
rationale: Need advantages of set-associative behavior (much improved hit rate) plus fast access time of direct-mapped; address paths needing extra logic levels are outside critical loop, mispredict cost only single cycle and predictors correct 85-100% for most apps, training via 2-bit hysteresis to avoid overtraining
outcome: Very high bandwidth instruction fetch even on non-cache-local code, can saturate L2 bandwidth with prefetches, predictable branches avoid misfetch penalty

title: Clustered integer execution with duplicated 80-entry register files
where_in_paper: Execution engine and Figure 6 integer execution pipes
decision: Split integer register file into two clusters each with duplicate 80-entry register file (plus 32 architectural), two pipes per cluster, combine to support 4-way integer issue; results broadcast with 1 extra cycle penalty between clusters
alternatives_or_rejected: Idealized unclustered 80-entry file with 8 read / 4 write ports and full bypass network; paper explicitly notes clustering makes design simpler and faster although costs extra cycle to broadcast from one integer cluster to the other
rationale: Unclustered 4-way file would be slow, high risk, large area and power; clustering provides much of implementation simplicity, lower risk, higher speed of 2-issue machine with performance of 4-way; critical path computations tend to stay on same cluster, and static fetch-position slotting equalizes utilization
outcome: Performance costs small - few percent vs idealized unclustered in most applications per paper; enables 500-600 MHz in 0.35um 6-metal with 15M transistors, 4 integer + 2 FP issues per cycle

title: Double-pumped 64KB 2-way data cache for dual memory references
where_in_paper: Internal memory system - Data path and Data cache
decision: Use 64KB 2-way set-associative data cache that is double-pumped: referenced twice each cycle once per clock phase, effectively operating at twice processor clock, to support any combination of two loads or stores per cycle without dual ports
alternatives_or_rejected: True dual-ported data cache or 8KB direct-mapped as in 21164; dual-port would be larger/slower and hurt cycle time
rationale: 21264 needs high bandwidth and low miss rate for both commercial and technical workloads; 64KB 2-way much lower miss rate than 8KB direct-mapped; double-pumping provides two ports with single physical array, keeping cycle time
outcome: Can service up to two out-of-order memory references per cycle, sustain >1.3 GBytes/sec on Stream, maintains 3-cycle integer load latency, with 32-entry LDQ/STQ and 8-entry MAF merging misses

title: Speculative memory ordering with load wait table and load hit/miss prediction
where_in_paper: Dynamic execution examples - Store/load memory ordering and Load hit/miss prediction
decision: Speculatively issue loads as early as possible before older stores, detect read-after-write hazard after issue via LDQ/STQ CAMs, squash load on mismatch and train load wait table to delay that load on subsequent executions until prior stores issued; plus predict load hit/miss with 4-bit counter (decrement 2 on miss else increment 1) to avoid squashing consumers of a miss - mini-restart of only 2 integer issue cycles instead of full pipeline restart
alternatives_or_rejected: Always delay loads until all older store addresses known (conservative inorder memory) or rely only on full pipeline restart on misspeculation; both would sacrifice significant performance for memory-intensive code
rationale: Register renaming cannot handle memory addresses until issue, so memory dependencies must be resolved dynamically; early load issue minimizes latency, but load miss would otherwise require restarting pipeline; predicting hit avoids overspeculation cost, wait table avoids repeated store/load order violations
outcome: Memory system appears inorder architecturally while capturing out-of-order performance; decoupled tag-only loads maximize bandwidth for misses; floating-point loads handled differently with 4-cycle latency allowing exact resolution without speculation
